children: England’s health spending watchdog on Thursday recommended Enhertu, a breast cancer therapy developed by AstraZeneca
for use across the country's National Health Service.

The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence on Thursday published final draft guidance related to the decision recommending the antibody-drug conjugate as a late-line option for adults with HER2-low advanced or metastatic breast cancer.

NICE previously deemed Enhertu too expensive for use within the NHS, at the price the companies offered, making it the only breast cancer drug the agency hadn't endorsed since 2018 for use within one of the largest public healthcare systems in the world.

However, in April, under a U.S.-U.K. drug pricing deal reached late last year, the agency raised the cost-effectiveness thresholds it considers to determine if a particular medicine delivers value for money.
The decision is expected to benefit ​nearly 1,000 women with breast cancer annually, AstraZeneca
said, adding that plans are underway to seek approval for access in Wales and Northern Ireland.
Enhertu is already available in more than 20 EU countries, and Scotland has made the drug available since 2023.

title: Astra-Daiichi breast cancer drug Enhertu recommended for NHS use in England
